column1: # Node-route corpus for `graph-lint.py --eval` (SPEC-0002 §6, ADR-0026). Seed round 7.37.0.
# Subject graph: the graph a fresh `install.sh claude-code` places into an empty project (75 nodes, no root,
# all seed-owned). The gate runs `--eval` over this file against that installed graph, never against a grown plant.
# Columns: task<TAB>required_ids<TAB>forbidden_ids<TAB>class
#   required_ids   comma list of node ids that must LOAD; "-" = none (an abstention is correct)
#   forbidden_ids  comma list of node ids that must NOT load; "-" = none
#   class          contract | paraphrase | adversarial | unknown-domain; classes are reported separately, never averaged
# Provenance. Every row except the tester's bait rows is copied verbatim (typos kept) from the round's 74-row
# measurement corpus (records-7.37.0/B-graph-routes.golden.tsv, data-ml spawn orchestrator.1.data-ml.2, authored
# 2026-10-01 over the steward plant): the 32 rows whose ids are all seed-owned, that is, every id they name is a node
# of the installed graph. That selection is mechanical and was not made by looking at any route.
# contract rows: copied from the curated router tables of the steward plant's index; self-consistency evidence only.
# paraphrase rows: owner prompts quoted verbatim, authored 2026-10-01 WITHOUT reading any target's load_when, and
#   NOT adjusted after any run. They must never be tuned, and no trigger may be tuned toward them.
# adversarial rows: the first is copied from B; the rest were added 2026-10-01 by the tester spawn
#   orchestrator.15.tester.8 against the installed graph, each baiting the resolve() mechanism named in the comment
#   above it (ADR-0026 context); the forbidden column names the baited node.
# unknown-domain rows: nothing in the graph is written for them; the correct outcome is an empty LOAD.
# --- contract (B, verbatim)
Who should do this? Which specialist?
